title: Starlink 10-38 Launch — B1069 (31st Flight); 607th Booster Landing on ASOG; SpaceX's 54th Orbital Mission of 2026
detail: SpaceX launched 29 Starlink V2 Mini broadband satellites from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on National Space Day (May 1) at 2:06:10 p.m. EDT (18:06:10 UTC). Booster B1069 flew its record-tying 31st mission, landing approximately 8.5 minutes after liftoff on drone ship 'A Shortfall of Gravitas' (ASOG) in the Atlantic Ocean — the 149th landing on that vessel and SpaceX's 607th cumulative booster recovery in history. The 29 satellites were deployed to low Earth orbit as part of the Starlink Group 10 shell, continuing the expansion of the polar-coverage Starlink constellation. This was the 43rd dedicated Starlink mission of 2026 and SpaceX's 54th total orbital flight of the year. Following deployment, the Starlink constellation stands at approximately 11,955 total launched and roughly 10,350 in orbit (10,334 working), maintaining broadband service to over 10 million subscribers across 160 countries.

media.caption: Falcon 9 B1069 launches Starlink Group 10-38 from SLC-40, Cape Canaveral, May 1, 2026 — SpaceX's 54th orbital mission of the year

title: Bloomberg: SpaceX Starship Development Spending Tops $15 Billion — $3B in 2025 Alone
detail: Bloomberg published a major investigation on May 1, 2026, revealing that SpaceX's total spending on Starship development has exceeded $15 billion — more than 37 times the ~$400 million spent developing Falcon 9. The report details that SpaceX invested approximately $3 billion in Starship R&D in 2025 alone and $1.8 billion in 2024, reflecting the accelerating pace of flight testing and hardware iteration as the company prepares for IFT-12. The spending figure underscores the scale of SpaceX's ambition to achieve airline-like rocket operations: Starship (Block 3 / V3) is designed for rapid full reusability with a target marginal cost per launch of under $10 million once the vehicle reaches operational cadence. Bloomberg notes that despite the massive investment, Starship has generated zero revenue to date — all costs are internally funded from Starlink and launch revenue. SpaceX's IPO prospectus, expected around May 15-22, is anticipated to disclose detailed Starship financial data for the first time, potentially revealing burn rates that could give investors pause at a $1.75 trillion target valuation.

media.caption: Bloomberg investigation reveals SpaceX Starship spending has exceeded $15 billion, with $3B spent in 2025 alone
